  "meta_commentary": "Pure-move refactor \u2014 zero behavior changes. The operation is mechanical but brittle: lose one test, lose one parametrize decorator, or accidentally touch a `megaplan/` source file and the parity checks will correctly fail. Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. Removing the helper block from test_megaplan.py during T3 would break every remaining test that references it by name. (4) Byte-for-byte for helpers: copy the block from `tests/test_megaplan.py:39\u2013232` verbatim. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. The `strict_schema` tests in test_megaplan.py are NOT duplicates of the similarly named ones in tests/test_schemas.py (different suffixes, different assertions) \u2014 preserve both sets. If `tests/test_execute.py` runs over ~1500 lines, split to `tests/test_execute.py` + `tests/test_execute_batch.py`, otherwise keep as one. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original. Do not modify test bodies to make them pass; the tests were green before the move, so any red after the move is a move error, not a test-correctness error.",

  "meta_commentary": "Pure-move refactor \u2014 zero behavior changes. The operation is mechanical but brittle: lose one test, lose one parametrize decorator, or accidentally touch a `megaplan/` source file and the parity checks will correctly fail. Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. Removing the helper block from test_megaplan.py during T3 would break every remaining test that references it by name. (4) Byte-for-byte for helpers: copy the block from `tests/test_megaplan.py:39\u2013232` verbatim. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. The `strict_schema` tests in test_megaplan.py are NOT duplicates of the similarly named ones in tests/test_schemas.py (different suffixes, different assertions) \u2014 preserve both sets. If `tests/test_execute.py` runs over ~1500 lines, split to `tests/test_execute.py` + `tests/test_execute_batch.py`, otherwise keep as one. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original. Do not modify test bodies to make them pass; the tests were green before the move, so any red after the move is a move error, not a test-correctness error.",

  "meta_commentary": "Pure-move refactor \u2014 zero behavior changes. The operation is mechanical but brittle: lose one test, lose one parametrize decorator, or accidentally touch a `megaplan/` source file and the parity checks will correctly fail. Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. Removing the helper block from test_megaplan.py during T3 would break every remaining test that references it by name. (4) Byte-for-byte for helpers: copy the block from `tests/test_megaplan.py:39\u2013232` verbatim. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. The `strict_schema` tests in test_megaplan.py are NOT duplicates of the similarly named ones in tests/test_schemas.py (different suffixes, different assertions) \u2014 preserve both sets. If `tests/test_execute.py` runs over ~1500 lines, split to `tests/test_execute.py` + `tests/test_execute_batch.py`, otherwise keep as one. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original. Do not modify test bodies to make them pass; the tests were green before the move, so any red after the move is a move error, not a test-correctness error.",

Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original.   "meta_commentary": "Pure-move refactor \u2014 zero behavior changes. The operation is mechanical but brittle: lose one test, lose one parametrize decorator, or accidentally touch a `megaplan/` source file and the parity checks will correctly fail. Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. Removing the helper block from test_megaplan.py during T3 would break every remaining test that references it by name. (4) Byte-for-byte for helpers: copy the block from `tests/test_megaplan.py:39\u2013232` verbatim. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. The `strict_schema` tests in test_megaplan.py are NOT duplicates of the similarly named ones in tests/test_schemas.py (different suffixes, different assertions) \u2014 preserve both sets. If `tests/test_execute.py` runs over ~1500 lines, split to `tests/test_execute.py` + `tests/test_execute_batch.py`, otherwise keep as one. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original. Do not modify test bodies to make them pass; the tests were green before the move, so any red after the move is a move error, not a test-correctness error.",

  "meta_commentary": "Pure-move refactor \u2014 zero behavior changes. The operation is mechanical but brittle: lose one test, lose one parametrize decorator, or accidentally touch a `megaplan/` source file and the parity checks will correctly fail. Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. Removing the helper block from test_megaplan.py during T3 would break every remaining test that references it by name. (4) Byte-for-byte for helpers: copy the block from `tests/test_megaplan.py:39\u2013232` verbatim. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. The `strict_schema` tests in test_megaplan.py are NOT duplicates of the similarly named ones in tests/test_schemas.py (different suffixes, different assertions) \u2014 preserve both sets. If `tests/test_execute.py` runs over ~1500 lines, split to `tests/test_execute.py` + `tests/test_execute_batch.py`, otherwise keep as one. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original. Do not modify test bodies to make them pass; the tests were green before the move, so any red after the move is a move error, not a test-correctness error.",

  "meta_commentary": "Pure-move refactor \u2014 zero behavior changes. The operation is mechanical but brittle: lose one test, lose one parametrize decorator, or accidentally touch a `megaplan/` source file and the parity checks will correctly fail. Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. Removing the helper block from test_megaplan.py during T3 would break every remaining test that references it by name. (4) Byte-for-byte for helpers: copy the block from `tests/test_megaplan.py:39\u2013232` verbatim. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. The `strict_schema` tests in test_megaplan.py are NOT duplicates of the similarly named ones in tests/test_schemas.py (different suffixes, different assertions) \u2014 preserve both sets. If `tests/test_execute.py` runs over ~1500 lines, split to `tests/test_execute.py` + `tests/test_execute_batch.py`, otherwise keep as one. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original. Do not modify test bodies to make them pass; the tests were green before the move, so any red after the move is a move error, not a test-correctness error.",

  "meta_commentary": "Pure-move refactor \u2014 zero behavior changes. The operation is mechanical but brittle: lose one test, lose one parametrize decorator, or accidentally touch a `megaplan/` source file and the parity checks will correctly fail. Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. Removing the helper block from test_megaplan.py during T3 would break every remaining test that references it by name. (4) Byte-for-byte for helpers: copy the block from `tests/test_megaplan.py:39\u2013232` verbatim. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. The `strict_schema` tests in test_megaplan.py are NOT duplicates of the similarly named ones in tests/test_schemas.py (different suffixes, different assertions) \u2014 preserve both sets. If `tests/test_execute.py` runs over ~1500 lines, split to `tests/test_execute.py` + `tests/test_execute_batch.py`, otherwise keep as one. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original. Do not modify test bodies to make them pass; the tests were green before the move, so any red after the move is a move error, not a test-correctness error.",

  "meta_commentary": "Pure-move refactor \u2014 zero behavior changes. The operation is mechanical but brittle: lose one test, lose one parametrize decorator, or accidentally touch a `megaplan/` source file and the parity checks will correctly fail. Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. Removing the helper block from test_megaplan.py during T3 would break every remaining test that references it by name. (4) Byte-for-byte for helpers: copy the block from `tests/test_megaplan.py:39\u2013232` verbatim. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. The `strict_schema` tests in test_megaplan.py are NOT duplicates of the similarly named ones in tests/test_schemas.py (different suffixes, different assertions) \u2014 preserve both sets. If `tests/test_execute.py` runs over ~1500 lines, split to `tests/test_execute.py` + `tests/test_execute_batch.py`, otherwise keep as one. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original. Do not modify test bodies to make them pass; the tests were green before the move, so any red after the move is a move error, not a test-correctness error.",

  "meta_commentary": "Pure-move refactor \u2014 zero behavior changes. The operation is mechanical but brittle: lose one test, lose one parametrize decorator, or accidentally touch a `megaplan/` source file and the parity checks will correctly fail. Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. Removing the helper block from test_megaplan.py during T3 would break every remaining test that references it by name. (4) Byte-for-byte for helpers: copy the block from `tests/test_megaplan.py:39\u2013232` verbatim. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. The `strict_schema` tests in test_megaplan.py are NOT duplicates of the similarly named ones in tests/test_schemas.py (different suffixes, different assertions) \u2014 preserve both sets. If `tests/test_execute.py` runs over ~1500 lines, split to `tests/test_execute.py` + `tests/test_execute_batch.py`, otherwise keep as one. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original. Do not modify test bodies to make them pass; the tests were green before the move, so any red after the move is a move error, not a test-correctness error.",

- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the mobile action-surface plan is technically incorrect for the current component structure. `submissioncarouselcard` hides `footercontent` below the `md` breakpoint (`src/components/submissioncarouselcard.tsx:219`), while `submissionscarouselpage` also hides the score panel on mobile via `asidecontent={<div classname="hidden md:block">...` and passes `hideactions` to `scorepanel` at `src/pages/submissionscarouselpage.tsx:250-263,347`. reusing that pattern for entrypage would leave mobile users with no navigation controls and no scoring controls. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: i checked the sign-in callback path again. `submissionslayout` already wires `usescoring(..., { onrequiresignin: () => pagemachine.dispatch({ type: 'open_sign_in_modal' }) })` at `src/pages/submissionslayout.tsx:38-40`, and `scorepanel` still has its own `onrequiresignin` prop. the revised step 4.2 is acceptable only if it explicitly rewires that prop to `pagemachine.dispatch`; otherwise removing local modal state would orphan the direct ui callback. the plan hints at this, but it remains easy to misread because the scoring-context callback and the scorepanel prop are separate mechanisms. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the new diff-helper proposal against the repo's existing execution-evidence semantics. `validate_execution_evidence()` in `megaplan/evaluation.py:109-175` uses `git status --short`, so untracked files count as real changed files today, but step 3 proposes `collect_git_diff_patch(project_dir)` via `git diff head`; by git behavior that will not include untracked files, so heavy review could miss exactly the newly created files that execute and review already treat as part of the patch. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

  "meta_commentary": "Pure-move refactor \u2014 zero behavior changes. The operation is mechanical but brittle: lose one test, lose one parametrize decorator, or accidentally touch a `megaplan/` source file and the parity checks will correctly fail. Four disciplines make this succeed: (1) never type `python -m pytest` \u2014 always `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`; the bare interpreter is 3.8 and will ImportError before collection. (2) Move-then-delete: as each test lands in its new home, delete it from `tests/test_megaplan.py` in the same edit. Duplicate function names across files inflate pytest's collected count and mask parity regressions. (3) Keep the conftest.py helpers duplicated with test_megaplan.py until T14 deletes the original \u2014 this is the intended resolution of FLAG-002. Removing the helper block from test_megaplan.py during T3 would break every remaining test that references it by name. (4) Byte-for-byte for helpers: copy the block from `tests/test_megaplan.py:39\u2013232` verbatim. No cleanups, renames, or signature adjustments \u2014 the helpers are consumed by every test file and silent changes propagate everywhere. Validate after each file: the per-file `pytest tests/test_<phase>.py -q` run takes seconds and pinpoints import/fixture mistakes while the blast radius is still tiny. Walk top-to-bottom through `tests/test_megaplan.py` so line-reference cross-checking stays easy. The file names `tests/test_types_schemas.py` and `tests/test_audits.py` are deliberate \u2014 `tests/test_schemas.py` and `tests/test_config.py` already exist and hold non-overlapping tests; do not merge into them and do not modify them. The `strict_schema` tests in test_megaplan.py are NOT duplicates of the similarly named ones in tests/test_schemas.py (different suffixes, different assertions) \u2014 preserve both sets. If `tests/test_execute.py` runs over ~1500 lines, split to `tests/test_execute.py` + `tests/test_execute_batch.py`, otherwise keep as one. On the final suite run: if a test fails, the fix is almost always a missing import, a wrong `tests.conftest` name, or a parametrize decorator that didn't travel with its function \u2014 grep the failing test name in the destination file and compare it against the original. Do not modify test bodies to make them pass; the tests were green before the move, so any red after the move is a move error, not a test-correctness error.",
